method.selection_policy: LLM-selected market-relevant items from news_digest.json; preserves source metadata and excludes noise.

framework.Equities: Broad equity/risk sentiment; market-moving mega-cap/AI allowed; low-signal single-stock noise excluded.
framework.Commodities: Physical commodity futures framework; supply disruption/demand strength positive; supply increase/demand weakness negative.
framework.FX: USD-centric basket; non-USD currency strength positive; USD/DXY strength negative.
framework.Rates: Bond-price framework; yields up/selloff/higher-for-longer negative; yields down/bond rally/cooler inflation positive.

Equities.title: Asian stock markets rebound on weak US data, lower oil prices, KOSPI surges almost 6%
Equities.summary: Asian stock markets reflect strong demand on Friday, as traders reconsidering hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) bets and lower oil prices due to easing geopolitical woes have lifted demand for risk-sensitive assets.
Equities.reason: Regional risk-on move tied to weaker US Fed rate expectations and lower oil risk premium — supports broad equity sentiment. High relevance because it reinforces cross-market risk appetite and dovish repricing themes.

Equities.title: S&P 500: Dovish repricing lifts breadth – Deutsche Bank
Equities.summary: Deutsche Bank strategists Jim Reid and colleagues note that a softer US jobs report reduced expectations for further Federal Reserve tightening in 2026, with just 30 bps of hikes priced by December.
Equities.reason: Clear macro driver: softer jobs data -> material downgrading of Fed tightening expectations, lifting market breadth. Very relevant for equities as it shifts the market regime toward lower-for-longer rates and broadens participation.

Equities.title: Dow jumps to record closing high after soft US jobs data, Nasdaq down with chip shares
Equities.reason: Market reaction to soft US jobs: cyclical/financials-led gains pushing indices to records while tech/chips lag — indicates rotation and improved risk appetite. Relevant as a cross-asset confirmation of dovish repricing impact.

Equities.title: US Stocks Erase Jobs Report-Related Gains as Semis Pull Back
Equities.reason: Shows sector-specific weakness (semiconductors) and profit-taking in tech amid the jobs-data bounce — negative for the AI/chip-led part of the market but lower relevance to the broad equity regime narrative.

Equities.title: Nvidia offers start-up customers chance to swap compute power for revenue share
Equities.summary: Nvidia says it will give start-ups the chance to swap access to compute power for a slice of future profits under a new program aimed at AI-focused firms.
Equities.reason: Reinforces AI leadership narrative and practical demand for Nvidia compute — positive for AI/software-capex complex and equity sentiment around tech leadership. Sector-level relevance moderate-high.

Equities.title: Microsoft commits $2.5 billion and 6,000 employees to new AI implementation unit
Equities.summary: Microsoft is the latest tech company to form a business focused on helping customers understand and implement artificial intelligence.
Equities.reason: Major-cap structural investment into AI adoption supports prolonged sector leadership and revenue visibility for large-cap tech — positive for growth/AI narrative and index leadership.

Equities.title: Surging Wall Street profit forecasts fuel fears of ‘earnings bubble’
Equities.summary: Analysts’ expectations for S&P 500 earnings are rising at fastest rate since rebound from Covid pandemic
Equities.reason: Rising earnings forecasts raise valuation and 'earnings bubble' risks — a material downside macro/structural risk to equities if forecasts disappoint. High relevance as it questions sustainability of the rally.

Equities.title: Tesla stock sinks 7% despite strong deliveries report, posting worst day in nearly a year
Equities.summary: Tesla is trying to recover from consecutive annual declines in vehicle sales that were partly caused by a consumer backlash against CEO Elon Musk.
Equities.reason: Large-cap idiosyncratic selloff that can sap tech/market confidence short-term. Relevant but lower weight for the overall equity regime since it's company-specific and tied to EV demand/management issues.

Equities.title: South Korean Stocks Jump 5% After Turbulent Week on AI Swings
Equities.reason: Regional rally driven by AI narrative — supports global tech/AI leadership theme and shows how AI flows are rotating into Asia. Useful confirmation of cross-border AI-led equity flows.

Equities.title: The Rotation Trade Is Back on Wall Street
Equities.reason: Macro/flow narrative: rotation from growth/semis into cyclicals/financials after data-driven repricing. Moderately positive for breadth and a signal of regime shift within the equity market.

Rates.title: Turkish Lira: Limited relief from June inflation – Commerzbank
Rates.summary: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose expects Turkey’s June Consumer Price Index (CPI) to show a modest disinflation surprise, with headline and core rates easing slightly and month-on-month inflation potentially below 1%.
Rates.reason: Modest disinflation in Turkey implies scope for lower nominal yields / easing local rate pressure — positive for Turkish bonds but country-specific and headline-limited, so moderate relevance.

Rates.title: U.S. job creation cools in June with payrolls growth of just 57,000; unemployment rate at 4.2%
Rates.summary: Nonfarm payrolls were expected to rise by 115,000 in June and the unemployment rate to hold steady at 4.3%.
Rates.reason: Significantly cooler-than-expected US payrolls materially reduce near-term Fed hike odds and support a bond rally (yields down). High macro importance makes this a high-relevance positive for rates (bond prices).

Rates.title: Dollar heads for weekly drop as jobs data dims Fed hike bets
Rates.reason: Market reaction to the US jobs print (weaker payrolls) is reducing Fed hike expectations — dollar weakness and lower US Treasury yields implied; clear cross-market signal supportive for bonds.

Rates.title: Federal Reserve: Minutes watched as Fed holds – Wells Fargo
Rates.summary: Wells Fargo Economics, led by Tom Porcelli and colleagues, expects the June FOMC minutes to clarify what might push a divided Committee toward further tightening, but still sees the Federal Reserve keeping the funds rate unchanged.
Rates.reason: Minutes that highlight what could tilt a split Fed toward more tightening are a potential hawkish pivot risk for rates (could push yields higher). This is a moderate-signal, market-watch item.

Rates.title: ECB to integrate non-financial credit claim portfolios into general collateral framework, phasing out temporary measures
Rates.reason: Operational GC-framework change (making certain collateral treatment permanent) improves market functioning/liquidity in euro repo and bond markets — supportive for euro fixed income (lower term yields); significant operational policy signal for rates/market plumbing.

Rates.title: Isabel Schnabel: Is inflation back?
Rates.reason: Senior ECB official questioning whether inflation is returning is a clearly hawkish thematic signal for euro area policy — raises the risk of further tightening/path-dependence and therefore upward pressure on yields.

Rates.title: AMP Says Bonds No Longer a Hedge, Cuts From Some Pension Funds
Rates.reason: Institutional shifts (pensions trimming bond exposure because bonds no longer hedge) imply structural selling/less demand for duration — a negative flow for bond markets that supports higher yields.

Rates.title: Japan’s Convertible Bonds Regain Favor as Rates Continue to Rise
Rates.reason: Headline explicitly notes rates are continuing to rise — reinforces ongoing higher-for-longer/ratcheting rates narrative (negative for fixed income). Japan-specific but echoes broader global rates pressure.

FX.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risks and softer payrolls – MUFG
FX.summary: MUFG’s Michael Wan notes that softer US non-farm payrolls and suspected FX intervention supported the Japanese Yen, pushing USD/JPY sharply lower. He highlights that weaker payrolls reduce the likelihood of a near-term Fed rate hike but do not clarify the broa
FX.reason: Intervention speculation + softer US NFP is a clear USD-weak/JPY-strong driver. High relevance because it ties FX moves to macro (Fed outlook) and potential central-bank action, which is market-moving for G10 FX.

FX.title: Japan’s Kihara: Closely monitoring market movements with high sense of urgency
FX.summary: Japan's Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara reiterates, during the European session on Friday, that the administration is closely monitoring FX moves and is ready to intervene when needed. Kihara also said on Tuesday that officials are always ready to take t
FX.reason: Official statement signaling readiness to intervene materially raises intervention risk — a direct, high-impact FX narrative that supports JPY and can drive large USD/JPY moves and volatility.

FX.title: Japanese Yen: Softer jobs data supports yen – Commerzbank
FX.summary: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay and Dr. Henry Hao note that weaker US non-farm payrolls and reduced Fed rate hike expectations weighed on the Dollar, supporting the Japanese Yen. USD/JPY fell sharply as markets priced a smaller cumulative hike by year-end and specul
FX.reason: Research-house confirmation that NFP-driven Fed repricing is boosting JPY. Reinforces broader JPY-intervention and USD-weakness narrative; moderate-high relevance as it amplifies the theme.

FX.title: Japanese Yen steadies as intervention risks rise, Fed hike bets ease
FX.summary: USD/JPY holds its position after experiencing volatility, trading around 161.10 during the Asian hours on Friday. The pair may depreciate as the Japanese Yen (JPY) could strengthen on rising speculation that Japanese officials are preparing another round of cu
FX.reason: Market note tying yen strength to rising intervention risk and eased Fed hike expectations — confirms near-term JPY-support narrative with plain FX-market implications.

FX.title: US Dollar Index: Jobs setback limits downside – ING
FX.summary: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes that softer US jobs data has weakened the Dollar but does not expect this alone to extend USD losses. He argues the report curbs hopes for two Federal Reserve hikes but is not weak enough for a major dovish repricing.
FX.reason: Analyst caution that NFP softness alone may not trigger large dovish repricing — a moderating/counter signal that limits the scale of USD weakness. Important for DXY positioning, hence moderate relevance.

FX.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: Falls to near 100.50 despite prevailing bullish bias
FX.summary: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, is extending its losses for the second successive day, trading around 100.60 during the early European hours on Friday.
FX.reason: DXY-focused forecast showing renewed downside after NFP — directly relevant to USD-driven FX flows. As a price-forecast piece, relevance is capped but still confirms USD-weakness narrative.

FX.title: Euro rises to near 1.1455 against US Dollar as weak US NFP batters US Dollar
FX.summary: The Euro (EUR) is up 0.16% to near 1.1455 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Friday. The EUR/USD pair gains as the US Dollar underperforms its peers due to a slight ease in hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate expectation
FX.reason: EUR benefiting from broad USD weakness after NFP. Relevant to USD-centric FX basket and reflects cross-market positioning (EUR/USD) tied to Fed repricing.

FX.title: British Pound holds firm near 1.3380 amid broad-based US Dollar weakness
FX.summary: The British Pound (GBP) appreciates against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, on track for a 1.3% appreciation this week, its strongest weekly performance in three months.
FX.reason: GBP strength is part of the broader USD-softness narrative. Material for G10 FX flows but less central than intervention/DXY items, so medium relevance.

FX.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Refreshes weekly high near 0.5725 as US Dollar weakens
FX.summary: The NZD/USD pair posts a fresh weekly high at around 0.5725 during the European trading session on Friday. The Kiwi pair reflects strength as risk-on market sentiment due to a slight cool down in hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations has improved the appe
FX.reason: Pair-specific forecast showing risk-on/carry flows as USD eases. Price-forecast/technical focus limits relevance despite clear USD-link.

FX.title: AUD/USD Price Forecasts: Aussie approaches 0.6950 with bullish momentum building up
FX.summary: The Australian Dollar (AUD) appreciates for the second consecutive day against a weaker US Dollar (USD) on Friday, still weighed by Thursday’s US Nonfarm Payrolls’ disappointment.
FX.reason: Aussie strength tied to the same USD-weakness/risk-on theme; technical/forecast nature keeps relevance capped.

FX.title: Canadian Dollar looks to extend recovery from YTD low on weaker USD, uptick in Oil prices
FX.summary: The USD/CAD pair struggles to capitalize on the previous day's modest bounce from a nearly two-week low and turns lower for the second straight day following a modest Asian session uptick to the 1.4200 neighborhood.
FX.reason: CAD recovering as USD weakens and oil ticks up; relevant because CAD is a commodity-linked G10 currency and participates in USD-driven flow shifts.

FX.title: Indian Rupee regains ground on lower oil prices, easing hawkish Fed bets
FX.summary: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens slightly higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday. The USD/INR pair drops to near 95.26 due to broader underperformance in the US Dollar, following the release of the weak United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for June
FX.reason: EMFX response to U.S. jobs-driven USD moves. INR appreciation reflects cross-border flows and DXY weakness — relevant for EMFX/flows but not as dominant as JPY/DXY themes.

FX.summary: Here is what you need to know on Friday, July 3:
FX.reason: Market roundup summarizing the dominant USD-weak/Fed-repricing theme — useful context with moderate relevance to FX flows and positioning.

Commodities.title: Gold: Softer US data boosts safe-haven demand – ING
Commodities.summary: ING’s commodities strategists highlight that Gold rallied after weaker US jobs data reduced fears of further Federal Reserve rate hikes. Lower Treasury yields and a softer Dollar improved the appeal of non-yielding assets.
Commodities.reason: Weaker US jobs data reduces Fed hike odds → lower real yields and softer USD, a clear bullish macro driver for gold. High relevance because rates/FX are primary gold drivers.

Commodities.title: Gold prices set for first weekly rise in a month as investors scale back Fed rate hike bets
Commodities.summary: The metal was boosted as investors scaled back their bets on a looming rate hike.
Commodities.reason: Mainstream confirmation that fading Fed-hike bets are supporting gold — supportive but somewhat redundant with other gold coverage, so moderate relevance.

Commodities.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD rises above $62.00 within broader bearish setup
Commodities.summary: Silver price (XAG/USD) jumps to the weekly high near $62.15 during the early European trading hours on Friday. The precious metal extends the rally as a weaker-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls ‌(NFP) report has reduced expectations of Federal Reserve (Fed) in
Commodities.reason: Silver rally tied to the same Fed/FX impulse as gold; article is a price/forecast piece (technical focus) so relevance capped at 0.8 per framework.

Commodities.reason: Reported draw in US commercial crude inventories and high refinery runs tighten crude balances → supportive for oil prices. EIA weekly data are market-relevant.

Commodities.title: TotalEnergies Offers Iraqi Oil to Asian Buyers as Supply Swells
Commodities.reason: Major seller (TotalEnergies) offering Iraqi crude to Asia signals rising flows and higher supply availability → bearish for oil prices; high relevance because it reflects physical flow changes.

Commodities.title: Citi Says Oil May Slump to $60 as the Hormuz Shock Fades Away
Commodities.reason: Sell-side forecast that the recent Hormuz risk premium is unwinding → downside risk to oil. Market-calling research is relevant but not definitive, so moderate-high relevance.

Commodities.title: Oil Steadies as More Supply Flows Through Strait of Hormuz
Commodities.reason: Increased flows via Hormuz reduce shipping-related risk premia and relieve a key supply concern → modestly bearish for oil.

Commodities.title: Oman walks a diplomatic tightrope over Strait of Hormuz fees, creating a ‘blind spot’ for markets
Commodities.summary: Oman is using strategic ambiguity as talks over possible Strait of Hormuz fees raise legal, diplomatic and oil market concerns.
Commodities.reason: Diplomatic ambiguity over transit fees could keep a small risk premium in oil markets; limited immediate supply impact so low relevance.

Commodities.title: U.S. refining capacity decreased during 2025
Commodities.summary: U.S. operable atmospheric distillation capacity, the primary measure of refinery capacity, totaled 18.2 million barrels per calendar day (b/cd) on January 1, 2026-down over 250,000 b/cd (about 1%) compared with January 1, 2025-according to our latest annual Re
Commodities.reason: Decline in US refinery capacity tightens product balances and can support crude differentials/prices; structural supply-side datapoint with moderate relevance.

Commodities.title: UAE's exit from OPEC+ reduced the group's share of crude oil production and capacity
Commodities.summary: On April 28, 2026, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) announced that it was leaving OPEC, effective on May 1. OPEC was formed in 1960 by Iraq, Iran, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela, with the stated objective to "coordinate and unify petroleum policies among Me
Commodities.reason: UAE departure reduces OPEC+ coordination capacity and the group's share of production/capacity — a modest structural bullish signal for crude, though outcome is uncertain.

Commodities.title: Copper Climbs With Industrial Metals as Rate-Hike Prospects Fade
Commodities.reason: Fading rate-hike prospects boost risk appetite and lower real rates, supporting industrial metals demand/pricing; copper is directly sensitive to macro and growth expectations.

Crypto.title: Bitcoin rises 4% to above $61,000 as inflation fears soften
Crypto.reason: Macro-driven BTC price rebound (softer inflation risk) reinforces risk-on flows into crypto; medium relevance as a market-wide momentum signal.

Crypto.title: Finally. $221 million flow into Bitcoin ETFs, ending a painful 10-day outflow streak
Crypto.reason: Significant institutional ETF inflow after multi-day outflows — strong positive for BTC liquidity and price discovery; high market impact for crypto asset class.

Crypto.title: US Treasury sanctions over 100 ISIS-K crypto addresses that moved over $1.4 million
Crypto.reason: Enforcement action demonstrates AML/ compliance capabilities and regulatory seriousness — modestly positive for institutional adoption and reputational risk reduction.

Crypto.title: Metaplanet buys another $170 million of bitcoin expanding treasury to 43,000 BTC

Crypto.title: Bitcoin's long-term holders have returned to accumulation
Crypto.reason: On-chain accumulation by long-term holders signals reduced selling pressure and underlying support for BTC — positive market-structure indicator.

Crypto.title: Bitwise says STRC selloff signals crypto cycle nearing a bottom, not Strategy’s breaking point
Crypto.reason: Asset-manager view framing recent selloff as cyclically bottoming supports a constructive narrative for recovery; moderate relevance to investor sentiment.

Crypto.title: JPMorgan says Strategy's bitcoin sales policy adds 'two-way risk' to crypto markets
Crypto.reason: Warning that concentrated corporate selling policies introduce liquidity and price downside risk — a negative idiosyncratic/structural signal with limited but real market impact.

Crypto.reason: On-chain metric showing a larger share of holders underwater increases potential selling vulnerability and short-term downside risk.
